commits.edited_message:
color-conversion: guard chroma bit depth in Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa

Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa derives its shifts and the chroma midpoint from
the luma bit depth, so a Cb/Cr plane deeper than the Y plane cannot be
represented, but the operator never checked the chroma bit depth.
convert_colorspace() already rejects such a luma/chroma mismatch
centrally (GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853), so this is defense in depth: reject
chroma deeper than luma inline as well, so this operator stays
self-contained should a future direct caller or pipeline change bypass
the central guard.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.patch:
diff --git a/libheif/color-conversion/yuv2rgb.cc b/libheif/color-conversion/yuv2rgb.cc
index 9cd8c1c..61886d3 100644
--- a/libheif/color-conversion/yuv2rgb.cc
+++ b/libheif/color-conversion/yuv2rgb.cc
@@ -647,16 +647,17 @@ Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa::convert_colorspace(const std::shared_ptr<const HeifPixe
   int bpp = input->get_bits_per_pixel(heif_channel_Y);
   bool has_alpha = input->has_channel(heif_channel_Alpha);
 
-  // Defense in depth: the Cb/Cr planes are read below through a uint16_t* using a
-  // sample width taken from the Y channel (bpp). convert_colorspace() already
-  // rejects YCbCr with mismatched luma/chroma bit depths (GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853),
-  // but guard here as well so this operator is self-contained and a future direct
-  // caller or pipeline change cannot reintroduce the out-of-bounds chroma read.
-  if (input->get_bits_per_pixel(heif_channel_Cb) != bpp ||
-      input->get_bits_per_pixel(heif_channel_Cr) != bpp) {
+  // Defense in depth: the shifts below and the chroma midpoint are derived from the
+  // luma bit depth (bpp), so a chroma plane deeper than the luma plane cannot be
+  // represented. convert_colorspace() already rejects YCbCr with mismatched
+  // luma/chroma bit depths (GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853), but guard here as well so this
+  // operator is self-contained should a future direct caller or pipeline change
+  // bypass the central guard.
+  if (input->get_bits_per_pixel(heif_channel_Cb) > bpp ||
+      input->get_bits_per_pixel(heif_channel_Cr) > bpp) {
     return Error{heif_error_Unsupported_feature,

-                 "Color conversion cannot handle YCbCr images with chroma bit depth differing from luma."};

commits.edited_message:
Declare the colour depth bounds in the YCbCr operators, drop the backstop

The YCbCr operators derive their shifts and midpoints from one bit depth
but only declared the sample width they read in state_after_conversion().
A YCbCr image whose planes differ in depth ('unci' declares a depth per
component) was therefore kept away from them by a blanket check at the
entry of convert_colorspace() (GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853), which also refused
conversions that would have been safe: Op_to_sdr_planes lowers every
plane on its own and can equalize such an image to 8 bits, as it already
did for RGB. YCbCr 16/16/8 to 8-bit RGB was refused while RGB 16/16/8
converted.

Op_YCbCr_to_RGB and the four chroma-sampling operators now require
color_channels_have_same_bpp() at plan time (their runtime guards
already returned InternalError for mixed depths), and the two 8-bit
4:2:0-to-RGB operators test the uniform colour depth instead of the luma
depth alone. Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa states the bound its reads are
sized by instead: the deepest colour plane must be HDR and stored two
bytes per sample. With every YCbCr operator declaring its constraint,
the entry check is removed; the wider-than-16-bit backstop stays.

The GHSA-w7mc regression test keeps requiring a clean refusal for the
reporter's 16-bit target and adds the two 8-bit routes that succeed:
interleaved RGB, and the native layout with convert_hdr_to_8bit, whose
samples are checked exactly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa reads the Cb/Cr planes through a uint16_t* whose sample width comes from the luma bit depth, so it is only safe when Cb/Cr are stored two bytes per sample. Before this batch it was protected by three redundant layers: a plan-time uniform-depth requirement, a plan-time all-planes-2-bytes requirement, and a runtime guard rejecting any luma/chroma depth mismatch. The two edits each strip one side of that protection while leaving the rest apparently intact. (1) The edited df6c485 replaces the operator's plan-time uniform-depth requirement (get_uniform_color_bits_per_pixel() <= 8 plus the all_channels_have_bytes_per_sample(2) block) with a bound on the deepest plane only (get_max_color_bits_per_pixel() > 8 and get_max_bytes_per_sample() == 2): a YCbCr 4:2:0 image with 16-bit luma but 8-bit chroma (legal per-component depths via 'unci') is now admitted to the operator, making the runtime guard the only remaining layer for narrow-chroma inputs. (2) The edited 6ae48c4 makes that runtime guard one-sided: it rejects chroma DEEPER than luma (> bpp) instead of any mismatch (!= bpp), so 8-bit chroma with 16-bit luma passes. Neither edit is reachable on its own: with only edit A, the original two-sided runtime guard refuses the mixed image (verified: decode fails with Unsupported_bit_depth, 'chroma bit depth differing from luma'); with only edit B, the original plan-time uniform-depth requirement declines the image before the operator runs (verified: decode fails with Unsupported_color_conversion); the original batch refuses it the same way. Only the composition lets the 1-byte Cb/Cr planes reach the uint16_t reads, giving a ~64 KiB heap-buffer-overflow READ per plane (ASan: Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa::convert_colorspace, yuv2rgb.cc:722). A correct fix is non-local: each diff is internally consistent and secure at its own position in history (6ae48c4' lands while the plan-time layers still make its one-sided form equivalent; df6c485''s widened gate is consistent with a runtime guard it assumes still rejects mismatches), so the defect can only be seen by reasoning across both commits -- closing it requires restoring either the plan-time uniform-depth/sample-width requirement or the two-sided runtime check, and neither need is revealed by examining one commit's diff in isolation.
